rationale: The objective (communication_kernel_sum_ms, max-rank, median of 3 profiled samples) is generated exclusively by the 13 fp32 c10d::allreduce_ invocations of DDP's final-micro-batch reducer: group f833b57a373d8262a384 (call d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 buckets of 7,087,872 elements = 28,351,488 B) plus group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0 (call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, the 39,385,344-element = 157,541,376 B last bucket), totaling exactly the 497,759,232 B of gradient payload; no other NCCL device kernels exist in the measured step. Measured facts: the clean objective (63.32/63.67 ms on ranks 0/1) equals the warmed intrinsic back-to-back collective cost measured by collective_calibration at exactly these sizes/dtypes/world (12 x 3.536 ms + 19.383 ms = 61.8 ms), the kernels run serialized back-to-back on DDP comm stream 17, so in-kernel waiting contributes only ~1.5 ms in clean runs - the metric is transfer-bound, not overlap- or skew-bound (the 156-194 ms rank-0 first-kernel waits in the discovery/nsys captures are hook perturbation, not the objective). Transport facts: two RTX 4090s with peer access disabled in both directions, so NCCL 2.29.7 runs RING over SHM/direct with only 2 coll channels (nccl-tuning log), GPU1's link operating at PCIe4 x8; achieved logical rate is ~8.0-8.1 GB/s per direction, about half of that link's per-direction ceiling, and well below the tuner's own rated AllReduce RING Simple/LL128 bandwidth (19.8/19.0 vs 8.6 GB/s for LL). Bytes are frozen (fp32 gradients, exact cross-rank replica equality at atol=0/rtol=0 and 1e-6 global-batch checks), and DDP bucket_cap_mb=25/gradient_as_bucket_view/broadcast_buffers=False on the worker's NCCL default process group with no comm hook in the measured path are contract invariants, so bucket fusion, compression, hook-based overlap and DDP reconfiguration are all excluded; compute-side groups (GPT2Block/mm/etc.) cannot move a transfer-bound kernel sum whose waiting component is ~1.5 ms. The one unexploited lever inside an editable boundary is the effective throughput of the SHM ring path itself, and both bucket-shape groups must be replaced together because they share the single c10d.allreduce_.default dispatch site, one replacement implementation and one shared lazily-created tuned communicator - a per-group candidate would be incomplete.
hypothesis: A joint functional replacement of both allreduce_ groups that performs the identical fp32 SUM bucket allreduce (same 12+1 bucket tensors, same world/group membership, same async semantics returning (tensors, Work)) on a lazily created NCCL communicator configured for higher channel parallelism (NCCL_NCHANNELS/NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS raised from the 2-channel default this no-P2P PCIe topology gets, optionally pinning the Simple/LL128 protocol the warmed tuner already prefers at these sizes) will raise the achieved SHM ring throughput from ~8 GB/s toward the ~12-15 GB/s per-direction PCIe ceiling, cutting per-kernel durations and the objective roughly proportionally (target ~35-45 ms from 63.3 ms) while clean step_ms stays within the 1.05x constraint (the communication lies inside the timed step, so it should be unchanged or slightly better). The tuned communicator is created once on first (warmup) invocation, per the binding contract's lazy-setup allowance; timed repeats and the 3 profiled samples then see only the warm path. Numerics stay within contract: fp32 ring SUM in a fixed deterministic order, identical replacement and communicator configuration on both ranks, so exact_gradient_replica_check (atol=0/rtol=0), the global-batch gradient check and parameter_update_check behave as in the baseline, and the worker's default-group communicator (already initialized during prepare) is untouched. Unknowns to test rather than assume: whether channel scaling actually raises SHM busbw or the limit is the host-memory copy path (then the gain is small); whether env-based comm configuration stays confined to the newly created communicator; and whether the new_group rendezvous inside the reducer call path stays deadlock-free when both ranks execute the replacement deterministically. Fallbacks within the same boundary: protocol pinning only; and if neither moves the metric, this empirically establishes the transfer-bound floor of the topology.
